# Build Instructions

FOSSynd uses CMake and needs only **SDL2** beyond a C++17
compiler. The **primary platform is Debian-based Linux** (Mint, Ubuntu); macOS
and Windows are supported and documented, not tested regularly.

## Build modes

| Mode | Flag | Needs SDL2? | Use for |
|------|------|-------------|---------|
| **Core + game** (default) | `-DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON` | Yes | Running and developing the game |
| **Core only** | `-DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF` | No | Unit tests, CI, logic-only work |
| **Sanitizers** | `-DFOSSYND_SANITIZE=ON` | No | Catching memory/logic bugs in `core` (developer/CI) |
| **Warnings-as-errors** | `-DFOSSYND_WERROR=ON` | Either | Keeping the tree warning-clean (developer/CI) |

Game logic lives in `src/core/` and builds without SDL2 (ADR-0002), so you can
work on gameplay with just a compiler.

## Running on very old hardware

The game must always run on low-end machines (ADR-0006, ADR-0008). Two things
guarantee that:

- The renderer is **software-capable** and the code uses no per-pixel effects on
  the critical path, so no GPU is required.
- A **low-spec profile** favours a small binary and a small window:

```bash
# Build the old-hardware profile (small, -Os, stripped)
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON -DFOSSYND_LOW_SPEC=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j

# Or run any build in low-spec mode at runtime (320x200 + software renderer)
./build/src/FOSSynd --low-spec
```

A `FOSSYND_LOW_SPEC=ON` build runs in low-spec mode automatically. CI builds this
profile on every change so it cannot bit-rot. If the game does not start on very
old hardware, that is a bug — please report it.

### The binary-size budget

The whole point of the profile is a **small** binary, so CI enforces a cap on it
(issue #222, AGENTS.md §1b, ADR-0008): the **stripped low-spec binary must be
<= 384 KiB**. As measured today, the low-spec build is ~375 KiB and the default
Release build is ~963 KiB, so the budget still fails loudly if the profile flags
are ever dropped or a heavy dependency sneaks in. The cap was raised from 288 KiB
when the third shared catalogue (`assets/data/vehicles.json`, #319/#342) left only
~2 KiB of headroom; to 336 KiB (issue #413) once `main` reached 318 KiB; to
352 KiB (issue #468) once `main` reached 334 KiB; and to 384 KiB (issue #477)
when the save/load wiring (#433) linked `core::CampaignSave` for ~24 KiB — more
than one 16 KiB step, so a single step would again have left a 2 KiB margin that a
single 4 KiB ELF page step would cross, and the next real PR would fail spuriously
rather than on a genuine regression.

The last breach was fixed by **reclaiming space rather than raising the cap
again**: two PRs that each passed alone merged seconds apart and crossed the cap
at 386 KiB, so the low-spec profile now builds with function/data sections
(`-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections`) plus linker `--gc-sections`, and gates
link-time optimisation on the compiler supporting IPO — together dropping the
binary by ~40 KiB (issue #512). The check now also **warns** (still exit 0) when
less than one ELF page (4 KiB) of headroom remains, so the next author reclaims
space or raises the cap deliberately instead of rediscovering a red lane.

> **The v1.0.0 size target is the whole game, not this binary.** ADR-0045 (the
> maintainer's directive) sets the v1.0.0 target at **the whole shipped game
> ≤ ~60 MiB** — the scale of a Syndicate Plus install — because targeting only
> post-2000 machines is fine; a low-spec *profile* is needed only if the game
> significantly exceeds that. Issue #524 re-scopes the gate accordingly; until it
> lands, the binary cap above is still enforced.

The CI `low-spec` job runs the check as a named step:

```bash
./scripts/check-size.sh build/src/FOSSynd
```

The same check is available locally as the `low_spec_binary_size` ctest, which
is registered only for a `FOSSYND_LOW_SPEC=ON` build:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -R low_spec_binary_size --output-on-failure
```

To change the cap, set `FOSSYND_SIZE_BUDGET_BYTES=<bytes>` (the default is
`393216`). Raise it only with a justification in the pull request — a larger
budget works against the reason the profile exists.

## Catching memory and logic bugs (sanitizers)

`FOSSYND_SANITIZE=ON` builds the engine-agnostic core and its tests with
**AddressSanitizer** and **UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer** (ADR-0015). Use it when
you change `src/core/` — it catches buffer overflows, use-after-free, leaks, and
undefined behaviour that ordinary tests miss:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build-san -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF -DFOSSYND_SANITIZE=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build-san -j
ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure
```

The option is **OFF** by default, so normal and low-spec builds are unchanged and
pay no runtime cost. The sanitizer profile is core-only (no SDL2 needed) and CI
runs it on every change (the `Sanitizers (ASan + UBSan, core)` job).

## Treating warnings as errors

The build already uses `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` and treats warnings as errors
"in spirit" (AGENTS.md golden rule 9). `FOSSYND_WERROR=ON` makes that literal by
adding `-Werror`, so a new warning fails the build instead of scrolling past:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON -DFOSSYND_WERROR=ON
cmake --build build -j
```

It is **OFF** by default (a warning still lets a normal build succeed) and works
with any other mode, so you can combine it with the low-spec or sanitizer
profiles. CI runs it in the `Warnings as errors (-Werror)` lane (issue #192),
so a warning cannot land on `main`.

## Packaging a release artifact

CPack (which ships with CMake) turns the `install()` rules into versioned,
installable packages (ADR-0017). It needs no extra dependency:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j
cmake --build build --target package
```

All three desktop platforms package from the same single-sourced `install()`
rules; only the generators differ. The artifact base name is
`FOSSynd-<version>-<system>` (`CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME`), so a version bump
changes every package name at once.

**Linux** — `TGZ` always, `DEB` where `dpkg-deb` is present:

- `FOSSynd-<version>-Linux.tar.gz` — portable; unpack anywhere and run
  `bin/FOSSynd`. The missions, string tables, catalogues, and example config sit
  in `share/fossynd/`, which the binary finds relative to itself.
- `fossynd_<version>_amd64.deb` — install with `sudo apt install ./fossynd_*.deb`.

**macOS** — `TGZ` plus a drag-and-drop `DMG` (`DragNDrop`, which uses the
`hdiutil` that ships with the OS):

- `FOSSynd-<version>-Darwin.tar.gz`
- `FOSSynd-<version>-Darwin.dmg` — open and drag `FOSSynd` to Applications.

**Windows** — a self-contained `ZIP` (no NSIS/WiX tooling needed):

- `FOSSynd-<version>-Windows.zip` — `FOSSynd.exe` and `SDL2.dll` under `bin/`,
  content under `share/fossynd/`; unpack and run `bin/FOSSynd.exe`.

The layout stays single-sourced with the `install()` rules; changing one changes
every package. The version comes from `project()` in the top-level
`CMakeLists.txt`, so a release bump changes the package names automatically.

**CI.** Linux packaging is the only hard gate and runs on every change. The
macOS and Windows lanes are `workflow_dispatch`-gated and non-blocking, so a
maintainer triggers them manually (a runner shortage can never redden `main`).

## Prerequisites

- CMake ≥ 3.15
- A C++17 compiler (GCC or Clang)
- Git
- SDL2 development files (only for the game target)

Install (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake git libsdl2-dev
```

Fedora: `sudo dnf install gcc-c++ make cmake git SDL2-devel`
macOS: `brew install cmake sdl2`
Windows (MSYS2 UCRT64): `pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-SDL2 git`

## Build and test (all platforms)

```bash
# Full build (core + tests + game)
./scripts/build.sh

# Or manually
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j

# Run the game
./build/src/FOSSynd

# Watch the attract mode (the squad fights on its own — good for demos)
./build/src/FOSSynd --demo

# Run the tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

## Playing the demo

There are two layers. The **tactical board** is a playable mission: eliminate
all enemy agents before your squad is wiped out. Press **`M`** (or start with
`--map`) to open the **campaign management screen**, where you tax territories,
fund research, buy equipment, and deploy missions to take the world map.

### Tactical board

| Input | Action |
|-------|--------|
| **Left click an agent** | Select that agent (highlighted) |
| **Shift + left click an agent** | Add/remove that agent from the selection |
| **Left-drag on the map** | Box-select every player agent inside the rectangle |
| **Keys `5`–`8`** | Select the 1st–4th living agent |
| **Ctrl + keys `1`–`4`** | Assign the current selection to control group 1–4 |
| **Keys `1`–`4`** | Recall control group 1–4 |
| **`A`** | Select the whole squad |
| **Left click the ground** | Order the selected agents to move (2-wide formation) |
| **Shift + left click the ground** | Append that tile to each selected agent's waypoint queue (walk a path) |
| **Right click an enemy (or left-click it)** | Order the selection to focus fire on that enemy |
| **`P`** | Use the selected agents' Compliance Beacons to recruit the nearest civilian in range |
| **`F`** | Release the selected agents' followers back into the crowd |
| **`H`** | Use a medikit on the selection (heal the most-wounded agent) |
| **`S`** | Raise a shield on the selection (absorbs the next hit) |
| **`C`** | Run a scanner pulse for the selection (marks nearby enemies) |
| **`[` / `]`** | Cycle the active drug bar (adrenalin / intelligence / physical) |
| **`;` / `'`** | Lower / raise the active drug bar for the selection (ADR-0043) |
| **`E`** | Hijack the nearest vehicle in range with the selection, or step out if the selected agent is already driving |
| **Arrow keys** | Scroll the camera |
| **`+` / `-` or the mouse wheel** | Zoom the view in whole steps (1x/2x/3x; wheel up = in) |
| **`F11`** | Toggle fullscreen / windowed |
| **`Space`** | Pause / resume the simulation (a `PAUSED` band shows while frozen) |
| **`M`** | Open the campaign management screen (needs campaign data) |
| **`R`** | Restart the mission (new seed) |
| **`Esc`** | Quit |

An agent under a focus-fire order shows a white/red reticle; the order clears
when you give that agent a move order, or automatically when the target dies.

### The campaign management screen

`M` (or `--map`) opens the **metagame**: a world of territories you tax for
income, fund research for, and buy equipment from. The tactical simulation is
frozen while the screen is up, and the campaign clock ticks instead.

| Input | Action |
|-------|--------|
| **Click a territory** | Select it (name, owner, mission, tax, and status show in the sidebar) |
| **`-` / `+`** | Lower / raise the selected territory's tax |
| **`D`** | Deploy the selected territory's mission with your bought loadout |
| **`B`** | Open the R&D shop (fund research, buy + assign equipment) |
| **`R`** | Recruit an agent (takes a fixed name from the region's pool) |
| **`F5`** / **`F9`** | Save / load the campaign (the in-play save path) |
| **`M`** | Return to the tactical board |
| **`Esc`** | Quit |

In the R&D shop: **Up/Down** move through the research tree and catalogue,
**Left/Right** pick the squad slot, and **Enter** funds a research node or buys
and assigns the selected gear. **`Esc`**/`B` closes it.

Win the deployed mission to claim the territory. Owning every region wins the
campaign (`CAMPAIGN WON`); when the campaign names a `finalMission` with
`winCondition: "final-mission"`, winning *that* board wins instead and a distinct
`FINAL CONFRONTATION WON` panel appears — even with neutrals left on the map.
Losing the syndicate shows `CAMPAIGN LOST`. The map then freezes — the end state
is final.

Your **progress survives quitting**: **`F5`** saves the campaign and **`F9`**
loads it on the map screen (the CLI takes `--save`/`--load`), and a new campaign
opens a **new-game screen** to name the syndicate and pick a logo.

Recruited civilians ("followers") trail their recruiter in cyan. They are not
combatants: they are never targeted, never fire, and never affect win/lose, so
a follower is a walking hostage rather than a soldier. The HUD shows the
current follower count.

The squad is the four green agents (bottom-left of the map); enemies are red.
Health bars float above every agent. The HUD shows the objective, the squad
roster (name, weapon, HP), and a win/lose banner.

Pale, unarmed **civilians** wander the streets. They are not targets: your agents
never shoot at them on their own, but stray shots near an enemy can kill them.
They flee when gunfire starts nearby. Civilian deaths you cause are counted as
**COLLATERAL** in the top bar and do not affect the mission outcome.

### Command-line flags

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `-h`, `--help` | Show the option list and exit |
| `-V`, `--version` | Show the version and exit |
| `--mission PATH` | Load the given mission file (overrides the config default) |
| `--campaign PATH` | Load the given campaign file (the world map) |
| `--config PATH` | Load the given config file; a missing file is a hard error |
| `--save PATH` | Save campaign progress to `PATH` on exit (the CLI save path) |
| `--load PATH` | Restore campaign progress from `PATH` at launch (a missing file is a hard error) |
| `--new-game` | Force the new-game screen (syndicate name + logo) before play |
| `--lang CODE` | Set the UI language (e.g. `en`, `de`) |
| `--demo` | Attract mode: the squad advances on the nearest enemy automatically |
| `--title` | Force the pixel-art title card (used to capture it headlessly) |
| `--map` | Start on the campaign management screen |
| `--low-spec` | Old-hardware mode: 320x200 window + software renderer (ADR-0008) |
| `--window WxH` | Set the window size in pixels (e.g. `1280x800`) |
| `--fullscreen` | Start fullscreen (desktop); `F11` toggles it at runtime |
| `--pause` | Start paused (frozen board); `Space` toggles it at runtime |
| `--zoom N` | Set the initial integer zoom level (1–3) |
| `--breach` | Breach every destructible wall before rendering (for rubble screenshots) |
| `--scan` | Fire a scanner pulse on the squad before rendering (for scanner screenshots) |
| `--shield` | Raise a shield on the squad before rendering (for shield screenshots) |
| `--drugs` | Take performance drugs on the squad before rendering (for drug screenshots) |
| `--vehicle` | Spawn a demo car and train before rendering (for vehicle screenshots) |
| `--bomb` | Plant a demo time bomb on the squad before rendering (for time-bomb screenshots) |
| `--headless` | Use the dummy video driver (no display needed) |
| `--frames N` | Run N frames then exit (must be a positive integer) |
| `--screenshot PATH` | Render one frame to a BMP and exit (with `--frames` first, simulates then captures) |

Unknown or incomplete options fail fast with a non-zero exit and a message on
stderr, rather than being silently ignored (issue #248); an explicitly named
`--config` or `--campaign` file that is missing is likewise a hard error
(issue #259).

### Headless verification flags

These run a self-check with no display and exit non-zero on failure; most are
wired into `ctest`.

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `--check-sprites` | Exit non-zero if the sprite sheet fails to bake (ctest `game_sprites`) |
| `--check-minimap` | Exit non-zero if the minimap panel or blips fail (ctest `game_minimap`) |
| `--check-selection` | Run the selection / control-group self-check and exit (ctest `game_selection`) |
| `--check-box-select` | Run the box-select self-check and exit (ctest `game_box_select`) |
| `--check-waypoints` | Run the shift-click waypoint-queue self-check and exit (ctest `game_waypoints`) |
| `--check-waypoint-path` | Run the queued-route overlay self-check and exit (ctest `game_waypoint_path`) |
| `--check-zoom` | Run the integer-zoom self-check and exit (ctest `game_zoom`) |
| `--check-fullscreen` | Run the fullscreen-toggle self-check and exit (ctest `game_fullscreen`) |
| `--check-pause` | Run the pause/resume self-check and exit (ctest `game_pause`) |
| `--check-rubble` | Run the breached-tile rubble self-check and exit (ctest `game_rubble`) |
| `--check-scanner` | Run the scanner-ping overlay self-check and exit (ctest `game_scanner`) |
| `--check-shield` | Exit non-zero if the personal shield overlay fails to draw (ctest `game_shield`) |
| `--check-drugs` | Exit non-zero if the drug-bar demo hook or the `B` bar spike fails (ctest `game_drugs`) |
| `--check-drug-bars` | Validate the three drug-bar HUD for the selection (ctest `game_drug_bars`) |
| `--check-drug-controls` | Drive the three drug-bar controls (`[`/`]`, `;`/`'`) and exit (ctest `game_drug_controls`) |
| `--check-bomb` | Validate the time-bomb demo hook (`--bomb`) and exit (ctest `game_bomb`) |
| `--check-audio` | Drive the real SFX synthesis, mixing, and event mapping with no device (ctest `game_audio`) |
| `--check-save-load` | Run the campaign save/load round-trip and exit (ctest `game_save_load`) |
| `--check-save-hotkeys` | Drive the in-game `F5`/`F9` save/load keys headlessly (ctest `game_save_hotkeys`) |
| `--check-newgame` | Drive the new-game name/logo decision and apply it to the campaign (ctest `game_newgame`) |
| `--check-objectives` | Validate the objective banner for every objective kind (ctest `game_objectives`) |
| `--check-campaign` | Drive the whole management loop (funds → tax → research → buy → deploy → win) and exit (ctest `game_campaign`) |
| `--check-deploy` | Drive the deploy round-trip (map → mission → result → map) and exit (ctest `game_deploy`) |
| `--check-lang [LOCALE]` | Run the UI string-table self-check and exit (ctest `game_lang`) |
| `--check-content [DIR]` | Validate the mission `weaponId`/`agentId` references against the catalogues in `DIR` (default `assets/data`) and exit; non-zero on a dangling reference (ctest `game_content`) |
| `--check-gadgets` | Run the tactical gadget hotkey self-check (`H`/`S`/`C`/`B`) headlessly and exit (ctest `game_gadgets`) |
| `--check-vehicle-input` | Run the vehicle input self-check (`E` hijack/exit, drive, mounted fire) headlessly and exit (ctest `game_vehicle_input`) |
| `--check-campaign-keys` | Headless guard: exit non-zero if a tactical hotkey leaks through the campaign map screen (ctest `game_campaign_keys`) |
| `--check-vehicles` | Exit non-zero if a live vehicle or a wreck fails to draw (ctest `game_vehicles`) |

### Core-only build (no SDL2 needed)

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

This is exactly what CI runs. If you only change `src/core/`, this is enough.

## Platform notes

### Debian-based Linux (primary)

The commands above work as-is. This is the reference environment.

### macOS

```bash
brew install cmake sdl2
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON
cmake --build build -j
./build/src/FOSSynd
```

### Windows (MSYS2)

From a **UCRT64** shell:

```bash
pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-SDL2 git
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON
cmake --build build
./build/src/FOSSynd.exe
```

## Troubleshooting

### `SDL2 not found` / `pkg_check_modules(SDL2 ...) failed`

Install the SDL2 development package (`libsdl2-dev`, `SDL2-devel`, or the MSYS2
package above). If SDL2 is installed in a non-standard prefix, set
`SDL2_DIR` or `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`. To skip the game entirely, build with
`-DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF`.

### The game window does not appear (headless machine / CI)

SDL needs a display. Use the headless flags, which select the dummy video
driver:

```bash
./build/src/FOSSynd --headless --frames 30
```

### No sound / `audio: disabled (...)` on stderr

Sound effects need an audio device (ADR-0040). When none can be opened — a
headless run, CI, no sound card, or a driver that cannot provide the baked format
— the game prints one `audio: disabled (...)` line and **runs silently**. This is
expected, not an error. To force a driver for testing, set `SDL_AUDIODRIVER`
(`dummy` for a no-op device, `disk` to write raw PCM to `sdlaudio.raw`). Music is
out of scope for v1.0.0; only SFX play. Issue #440.

### Clean rebuild

```bash
rm -rf build
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON
cmake --build build -j
```

See [`DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md`](DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md) for editor and
IDE setup.
